content:
I recently tried out a series of new MagSafe wallets, and they are increasingly looking like traditional wallets. The latest one I've tried is the Vinich MagSafe wallet, which comes in over 15 colour options. It looks like a traditional bifold wallet, and its design complements leather iPhone cases without any clash — it really feels like an extension of your iPhone case.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers breaks down the latest happenings in the MagSafe and wireless charging industry, helping you get the most out of your wireless-charging-capable Apple devices.

Colour options

The manufacturer has clearly been meticulous about colours, offering black, green, brown, and even purple, among others — all with a worn, vintage feel that pairs harmoniously with leather cases instead of clashing. Beyond these, there are countless other colours to choose from. Vinich also offers a Desert Titanium finish; if you prefer not using a case, this colour is a perfect match for your iPhone.

Wallet capacity

Vinich advertises three card slots and states that depending on card thickness, you can actually fit three to five cards. For everyday use, one driver's licence, a couple of credit cards, and a work access card usually suffice. Behind the card slots, there's also space to fold and tuck in a couple of notes. I find this surprisingly practical for such a compact wallet, and I try to carry around US$20 in cash with me.

The card slots are lined with RFID-blocking material, and the entire interior is lined with microfibre so your cards don't constantly rub against fabric. The magnet is reasonably strong — I've used stronger ones, but also far weaker ones.

Three things to know before you buy

First, this is synthetic leather, not genuine leather. It features scratch resistance and reinforced stitching, which is reasonable at this price point, but if you plan to pair it with a genuine leather case, bear in mind that the two materials may not match perfectly. Vinich recommends conditioning the wallet every three to six months.

Second, when taking ultra-wide or macro photos, it may gradually drift into the camera's frame. On most iPhones, it sits below the camera, but for close-up shots, you're best off removing it to make sure it's not obstructing the lens at all.

Lastly, it cannot be used as a stand, even though it might look like it could. The cover is intentionally designed to be fairly soft to reduce pressure on the magnetic ring, so if you want a wallet that can prop up your iPhone at an angle for calls or watching videos, this one isn't for you.

Wrapping up

At under US$25, the colour options alone make it worth a look if you've been searching for a wallet that pairs well with your beautiful leather case. Most MagSafe wallets are designed to be as understated as possible, but this one is designed to complement your case — both in feel and appearance, it still resembles a traditional wallet you could take out and use on its own. It would be great if a Find My tracking option could be added in the future.

You can pick up this Vinich MagSafe wallet on Amazon or directly from the Vinich website.
